chapter: Sidemen, the Hampton years, race and money
title: Dorian Mingus and Jimmy Rowles
summary: Johnson saw Dorian explain himself to Rowles after the quarrel; Dorian is 19.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: I was very impressed with Dorian. Nice, upstanding boy. Made quite an impression on Jimmy Rolls.
Oh, yeah? Who told you that?

I was there. Jimmy came over and sat at our table. He was a little in a state of shock, as a matter of fact. But then Dorian came over and apologized, and I thought he did it very manfully, very well.
Not apologized, he was explaining. He didn't apologize at all. But he said, 'I'm sorry I had to do

that, and I hope you'll understand and you'll shake my hand." And Jimmy wouldn't shake his hand. And finally, as he was walking away, he turned and said, "Well, if that's the way you feel about it, I have said the way I feel."
(inaudible) has nothing to do with my music."

He was very -- he handled it very well. Funny, I saw him come in, I didn't know who he was. And you hadn't gotten there yet, and I noticed him. I said, that's a kid who has some sense of his own importance, because he was standing there, looking around, very manfully. How old is he now?
Nice boy. Have they gone back to the coast now?
